name: QUEUE
description: A paid slot market for one FIFO agent-work queue. An urgent job buys earlier positions; every displaced job is paid its published per-second ask and must still meet its stated deadline, or the NEAR contract refuses the purchase.

hostedDemo.expect: Kestrel's urgent job jumps four places; Mira, Atlas, Vale and Juno are paid 0.00504, 0.00696, 0.00432 and 0.00372 NEAR; the receipt ends at "4 of 4 crossed promises kept"
hostedDemo.how: Static build (npm run build:pages). The ledger engine in packages/ledger runs in the browser tab; there is no backend and no wallet. The Season and Proof sections read NEAR testnet and the published proof records.

status: hackathon build; NEAR testnet only; not audited
externalLlm: none in the local demo and the v1 proof; the v2 season uses NEAR AI (Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8) for the agents and the worker
apiKeyRequired: no, to run the demo or to re-check any proof; a NEAR AI key is needed only to run a new season

cast.note: Seven roles in one server for the local demo; the testnet proof uses separate signing accounts. The auditor is console-only.

contract.sourceNote: The live proof is tied to the deployed wasm, and npm run build:contract on this tree reproduces the live code hash.

proof.episodeA: 5 of 5 jobs on time; 4 displaced and paid; 4 credits withdrawn
proof.episodeB: 1 refused jump; 2 of 2 jobs on time

counterfactuals.note: replays of the same jobs; within 0.5 s of the measured worker gap the three rules stay within a job or two of each other

sweep.note: simulator with a scripted policy; rules checked against the contract by the sim_parity test

tests.contractNote: 37 v1 + 62 v2 + 95 v3 tests on this tree; run npm run verify on the submission commit for the authoritative output.

methods.invariants: random histories (proptest): 48 per run, a 600-history run passes; each quote is checked against the rule worked out independently from the public queue
methods.differential: Rust contract replayed against the TypeScript rules: 20 histories / 1,284 steps committed, a 300-history / 24,866-step run agrees
methods.sweep: 300 simulated seasons: 0 of 3,464 moved jobs late; +1.19% on time vs FIFO
methods.mutation: cargo-mutants on the money, deadline and queue functions: 92 of 95 viable mutants caught, 3 equivalent
methods.plantedBugs: 8 of 8 caught by the unit, invariant and differential suites, each on its own (data/season/planted-bugs.json)
methods.reproducibleBuild: npm run verify:v2-deployed (byte-for-byte on macOS/Apple silicon, the deployer's platform, under any cargo home; the compiled wasm is host-dependent, so a Linux host reports a different build)
methods.hostedConsole: npm run verify:pages: the static build driven end to end in headless Chromium (one click, four agents paid, 4 of 4 promises kept, no backend)

verify.note: No wallet, no RPC, no API key. Without Rust the contract gate is skipped and the output says so. Includes secret scan, artifact reproduction, a scenario poll of up to 30s, and a drain of up to ~70s.

exitCodes.0: the hosted console ran the full scenario in a headless browser with no backend

limits.localApiAuth: none by default; binds 127.0.0.1; optional x-operator-token
limits.storage: caller-paid non-refundable deposits (deployed contract: 0.0125 NEAR per job; 0.003 + 0.003 per displaced NEAR per purchase)
disclosedStorageEdgeCases: C1 priority deposit shortfall for 1-3 displaced jobs with 64-byte accounts
C2 largest terminal job record can exceed its deposit
C3 failed native payout does not automatically restore the credit
limits.admin: v1 and v2: no built-in upgrade API and no timelock. v3: 24 h timelock on admin methods and upgrades. Every contract account retains a test FullAccess key that can redeploy directly and move the account balance; no multisig

cutoffSensitivity.note: Same seed; four displaced is a 5s start preference, not a deadline result. At 34s the urgent deadline binds and the result is two.

rules: operator stake (minimum 0.5 NEAR) pays a promised job that misses or fails: priority spend plus reward, as far as the stake goes
no new work when the stake is below the minimum or the operator has not called the contract for 180 s
the stake cannot be withdrawn and the operator cannot be replaced while a job is queued or running
only accounts the operator approved can submit (closed pilot: the eight season accounts); others are refused before anything is charged
a model job is paid only for a model-signed answer
ask raises take effect 30 s later; cuts are immediate
storage deposits are credited back whole when a finished job is released, less only bytes that stay in the contract
24 h timelock on the contract's admin methods and its own upgrade method
limits: the contract account still holds a test FullAccess key that can redeploy the code directly, outside the timelock
compensation is capped by what is left of the stake; the minimum stake is a floor, not a reserve per job
two approved accounts acting together can still make the operator pay a priority refund
v3.verify: npm run verify:v3 (read-only, no keys); npm run verify:v3-deployed (reproducible build)

client.mcp: npm run queue:mcp (stdio, 12 tools, per-call spend cap QUEUE_MCP_MAX_SPEND_NEAR)
